record.title: Bonsai 2 27B whitepaper reports roughly three-quarter retention on two agentic coding benchmarks
record.summary: PrismML’s September 17, 2026 whitepaper reports Ternary Bonsai 2 27B at 52.8 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 60.8% resolved on SWE-bench Verified, compared with 69.7 and 80.6 for Qwen3.8-27B FP16. The paper says the Terminal-Bench run used Terminus-2 on 89 tasks with one attempt each, while SWE-bench Verified used mini-swe-agent on all 500 instances. These two agentic results are separate from the paper’s 20-benchmark aggregate, where Bonsai 2 scores 83.9 versus 85.4 (98.2% retention). This is a bounded vendor-reported quality tradeoff, not independent validation; checkpoint hashes, run traces and independent reproduction remain open.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: PrismML’s September 17 Bonsai 2 27B whitepaper reports scores of 52.8 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 60.8% resolved on SWE-bench Verified, versus 69.7 and 80.6 for its Qwen3.8-27B FP16 comparator. The paper describes these as separate agentic benchmarks, outside the 20-benchmark suite behind its 83.9 versus 85.4 aggregate (98.2% retention) headline.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper says Terminal-Bench 2.1 used Terminus-2 with one attempt on all 89 tasks, eight concurrent trials, and an 80,000-token output budget per turn; SWE-bench Verified used mini-swe-agent on all 500 instances and reports resolved rate. The two evaluations ran on an identical Harbor-driven agent framework; detailed per-instance results or independent reproduction were not inspected.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction or instance-level audit of the reported Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE-bench Verified scores was performed. The whitepaper gives benchmark denominators and agent protocols but no audited run traces in this review.
This review did not verify the exact checkpoint hashes or independently confirm that the compared Bonsai and FP16 artifacts share the stated model lineage.

brief.importance_rationale: If the vendor-reported gap holds, it materially qualifies a near-lossless compression headline for long-horizon coding agents: the roughly 6 GB model retains about three quarters of the Qwen3.8-27B FP16 scores on two agentic software-engineering evaluations. The results are consequential for local deployment choices but remain first-party and unreproduced.
limitations: The results and protocol are reported by PrismML in its own whitepaper; no independent reproduction was inspected.
The paper’s main 20-benchmark aggregate reports 83.9 versus 85.4, but Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE-bench Verified are separately reported and excluded from that 20-benchmark suite.
This review did not inspect checkpoint hashes, per-instance result artifacts, or uncertainty intervals.
Terminal-Bench reports one attempt per task on 89 tasks; SWE-bench Verified reports resolved rate across 500 instances.

technical.claimed_result: PrismML reports Terminal-Bench 2.1 52.8 vs 69.7 and SWE-bench Verified 60.8 vs 80.6 for Bonsai 2 27B vs Qwen3.8-27B FP16. The separate 20-benchmark suite reports 83.9 vs 85.4 (98.2%).
technical.demonstrated_result: The primary whitepaper at the vendor’s official repository contains these reported scores and describes the benchmark setup. No independent confirmation of the scores or underlying runs was performed.
technical.mechanism: Ternary Bonsai 2 27B is evaluated against its Qwen3.8-27B FP16 comparator using Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE-bench Verified agent scaffolds, apart from the 20-benchmark aggregate.
technical.regime: Vendor-reported Terminal-Bench 2.1 using Terminus-2 on 89 tasks with one attempt each and eight concurrent trials; SWE-bench Verified with mini-swe-agent on 500 instances. The paper states both are driven by Harbor.
technical.reproducibility: The primary whitepaper and protocol are public; this review did not independently run the benchmarks, inspect per-instance traces, or verify checkpoint hashes.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper directly compares Bonsai 2 27B to Qwen3.8-27B FP16 on both agentic benchmarks; no other low-bit baseline is reported for these two task-specific scores.

brief.title: Bonsai 2 27B whitepaper reports roughly three-quarter retention on two agentic coding benchmarks
brief.why_it_matters: A small 27B-class model can preserve most of a broad 20-benchmark average while showing a materially larger reported drop on long-horizon coding agents. Separating the agentic tasks from the aggregate helps deployment decisions account for workload-specific quality. The exact scores remain vendor-reported pending reproduction.
